messages:
maria: Quick follow-up on the gateway inflight-state handshake we prototyped. Canary showed duplicate midstream retries when edge applied local retry + resume. Observations and proposals below.

aj: Can you paste the minimal logs you saw? Curious about how the retry id flowed.

maria: Yep — here's the chunk where duplicate tokens arrive after resume:

```
[ingress] recv id=0x7f2a client-req-id=abc123 seq=1
[proxy] forward id=0x7f2a upstream-id=U-9 seq=1
[ingress] resume id=0x7f2a resume-offset=512
[ingress] recv id=0x7f2a client-req-id=abc123 seq=1  <-- duplicate after resume
```

maria: Looks like ingress considered the post-resume frames a new attempt and didn't dedupe by original transaction id.

tung: The root tradeoff: do we make the request-id client-provided (best dedupe) or server-assigned (simpler to guarantee uniqueness across proxies). With resumed streams we need a stable canonical id that survives the handshake. Proposal: split identity into two fields — orig_tx_id (stable across lifetime) + attempt_id (ephemeral per connection). Use orig_tx_id for dedupe.

rachel: That solves correctness but increases state: proxies must remember orig_tx_id -> seen-offsets map for a TTL. Memory cost = #inflight * checkpoints_per_stream. Suggest windowed checkpointing (keep only last N offsets) and expire faster for small requests. Also consider a bloom filter for large fanout to save memory at false-positive cost.

samir: Minimal protocol change I'd advocate: include these in the resume handshake headers and trailers, e.g.:

```
Resume-Orig-Tx-Id: 9876e5
Resume-Attempt-Id: a1b2c3
Resume-Offset: 512
```

samir: On proxies that can't understand resume headers, default to previous behavior (full resend). We'll gate with feature flag for canary.

aj: What about gRPC-web + browser clients? They rarely set custom ids. We should fall back to server-assigned orig_tx_id at initial connect (returned in 101/early response) and require clients to echo it on resume.

maria: Nice. Observability follow-ups: we should 1) add a span tag resume=true and orig_tx_id to traces, 2) emit metric resume_duplicate_count and resume_handoff_latency. That will help diagnose regressions.

tung: Agreed — also add a histogram for resume-window-size (bytes between checkpoint and resume) so we can tune default checkpoint frequency.

rachel: I'll own a small eval harness to simulate resumable streaming across flaky connections and measure memory/CPU for the windowed checkpoint vs bloom filter approaches.

maria: Thanks — can we sync tomorrow in the arch huddle? @rachel @tung please bring rough numbers. I'll open an RFC follow-up doc with the header examples and a compatibility matrix.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout 7% -> 20% for service edge-proxy-resume (build 2026.03.21) started by @ci.

maria: Perfect, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
